([[Blairstown, New Jersey]]) | college = * [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] (2022–2024) * [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2024–2026) | draft_year = 2026 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 41 | draft_team = [[Miami Heat]] | career_start = 2026 | years1 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team1 = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | years2 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team2 = →[[Oklahoma City Blue]] | highlights = * 2× Second-team [[List of All-SEC men's basketball teams|All-SEC]] (2025, 2026) }} '''Otega Oweh''' (born June 21, 2003){{Cite web |title=Otega Oweh Player Profile, Kentucky - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Otega-Oweh/Summary/176073 |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=basketball.realgm.com |language=en}} is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. == High school career == Oweh attended Rutgers Preparatory School in Somerset, New Jersey where he played for esteemed head coach Matt Bloom. Rutgers Prep nurtured him defensively before transferring to [[Blair Academy]] in [[Blairstown, New Jersey]].{{Cite web |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |date=2021-11-10 |title=Blair Academy's Otega Oweh inspired by older brother's work ethic, path to the NFL |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2021/11/blair-academys-otega-oweh-inspired-by-older-brothers-work-ethic-path-to-the-nfl.html |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=nj }} He helped lead Team Final to a 17U [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League|Peach Jam]] title, totaling 17 points and five rebounds in the championship game.{{Cite web |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |date=2021-07-25 |title=N.J. guards Otega Oweh, Corey Floyd Jr. help lead Team Final to prestigious Peach Jam championship |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2021/07/nj-guards-otega-oweh-corey-floyd-jr-help-lead-team-final-to-prestigious-peach-jam-championship.html |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=nj }} A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], Oweh committed to play college basketball at the [[University of Oklahoma]].{{Cite web |last=Gallen |first=Daniel |date=2021-10-01 |title=4-star Otega Oweh picks Oklahoma over Nittany Lions |url=https://www.pennlive.com/pennstatefootball/2021/10/penn-state-mens-basketball-recruiting-4-star-otega-oweh-picks-oklahoma-over-nittany-lions.html |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=pennlive }} == College career == '''2023-2024 season''' After playing sparingly as a freshman, Oweh started 28 games as a sophomore, averaging 11.4 points and 3.8 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |last=Russell |first=Tyler |title=MENTAL GAME: Otega Oweh brings grit and determination to succeed into Kentucky men's basketball season |url=https://kykernel.com/107610/sports/mental-game-otega-oweh-brings-grit-and-determination-to-succeed-into-kentucky-mens-basketball-season/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=Kentucky Kernel}} At the conclusion of his sophomore season, he entered the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]].{{Cite web |last=Sulley |first=Colton |title=OU basketball: Sooners guard Otega Oweh plans to enter NCAA transfer portal, per report |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/college/sooners/2024/03/25/ou-basketball-otega-oweh-plans-to-enter-ncaa-transfer-portal-oklahoma-sooners/73096152007/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=The Oklahoman }} '''2024-2025 season''' On April 27, 2024, Oweh announced his decision to transfer to the [[University of Kentucky]] to play for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]].{{Cite web |last=Black |first=Ryan |title=Otega Oweh joins Mark Pope and Kentucky basketball from Oklahoma via transfer portal |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2024/04/27/kentucky-basketball-roster-otega-oweh-transfer-portal-recruiting-mark-pope/73316909007/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=The Courier-Journal }} In his Kentucky debut against [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State]], he scored a team-high 21 points.{{Cite web |last=Clabes |first=Jacob |date=2024-11-06 |title=Jamie Vaught: Kentucky junior guard Otega Oweh could make big impact for Wildcats this season |url=https://nkytribune.com/2024/11/jamie-vaught-kentucky-junior-guard-otega-oweh-could-make-big-impact-for-wildcats-this-season/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=NKyTribune }} In his first season with Kentucky, Oweh emerged as the team's leading scorer.{{Cite web |last=Black |first=Ryan |title=Kentucky's Otega Oweh always was athletic. Then he added consistency. It's a winning combo |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2025/02/20/kentucky-basketball-otega-oweh-mark-pope-sec-standings/78102316007/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=The Courier-Journal }} Oweh began his junior season with 26 consecutive games scoring in double figures.{{Cite web |last=Roberts |first=Ben |title=Otega Oweh just had his worst game as a Kentucky Wildcat. His next one could get weird |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article300880604.html}} On February 26, 2025, Oweh scored Kentucky’s final 18 points, set a new career-high with 28 points, and scored the game winner with six seconds remaining against his former team, the [[Oklahoma Sooners]].{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/kentucky-oklahoma-score-991401a318758d2a431f142f56394933|title=Oweh scores 28 points, hits winner against former team as No. 17 Kentucky tops Oklahoma 83-82|first=Cliff|last=Brunt|website=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 26, 2025|access-date=March 14, 2025}} Four games later in the second round of the [[2025 SEC men's basketball tournament]], Oweh scored 27 points and made another game winner with 0.5 seconds left against Oklahoma.{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/oklahoma-kentucky-score-1a42e8e9e81dcc23aff0652953ddd26e|title=Otega Oweh scores last shot again as No. 15 Kentucky sends Oklahoma home from 1st SEC Tourney |first=Teresa|last=Walker|website=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 14, 2025|access-date=March 14, 2025}} Oweh was named Second Team All-SEC {{cite web|url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2025/03/10/otega-oweh-named-all-sec-second-team-by-league-coaches/|title=Otega Oweh Named All-SEC Second Team by League Coaches|website= [[UK Athletics]]|date=June 23, 2026|access-date=June 23, 2026}} and averaged 16.2 points per game, 4.7 rebounds per game, 1.7 assists per game, and 1.6 steals per game. '''2025-2026 season''' Oweh initially declared for the [[2025 NBA Draft]] while preserving his college eligibility. However, he removed his name from the draft pool and announced his return to Kentucky on May 28, 2025. On February 21, 2026, he had a regular-season career-high 29 points against the Auburn Tigers. On March 20, 2026, he had a career-high 35 points in an overtime win against the Santa Clara Broncos in the first round of the NCAA Tournament, including a buzzer-beater 3 to send the game to overtime, before the Wildcats lost to the Iowa State Cyclones in the second round. Oweh finished his career at Kentucky with 1,255 points, becoming the fastest player in the school’s history to reach 1,000 points as a Wildcat. Additionally, he scored 10 or more points in all but one game he played in, and was named Second Team All-SEC for the second consecutive year. == Professional career == On June 24, 2026, Oweh was selected by the [[Miami Heat]] with the 41st overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]] then immediately traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] with cash considerations for pick 37 ([[Ryan Conwell]]).{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-the-draft-rights-to-ryan-conwell|title=HEAT ACQUIRE THE DRAFT RIGHTS TO RYAN CONWELL|website=nba.com|date=June 24,
